supported_scope: Branching with /fork command to create parallel conversation branches; session management with /resume to switch or restore branches; interactive diff viewer supporting Git, Mercurial, and Jujutsu repositories; workspace scoping to local repository directories
unsupported_scope: Explicit automated pull request creation or management
required_setup: Use /fork to create branches, /resume to switch or restore sessions; configure workspace permissions and sandboxing for safe command execution; optionally create GEMINI.md or AGENTS.md rule files for workspace standards; use /diff to review changes interactively
constraints: Branching and session management are limited to conversation sessions, not full Git branch operations
Diff viewer supports Git, Mercurial, and Jujutsu but does not imply automated pull request or deployment support
Sandboxing and permissions must be configured to allow necessary file and command access
No explicit commands or hooks documented for automated CI/CD or deployment workflows

evidence.section: Managing conversations > Branching with /fork > Forking workflow
evidence.quote: Type /fork inside the prompt panel and press Enter . The CLI allocates a new unique session ID and duplicates your existing workspace state and agent thread. Your active terminal switches immediately to the new branch.
evidence.claim: Supports branching of conversation sessions via /fork command

evidence.quote: /fork command clones your entire conversation history up to the current turn into a new, independent session.
evidence.claim: Enables parallel experimentation with branched conversation sessions

evidence.section: Diff command (/diff) > Interactive diff viewer panels > Navigation and controls
evidence.quote: The diff viewer operates in three modes... VCS mode : Shows a list of all modified and untracked files in your active workspace: Supports Git, Mercurial (Hg), and Jujutsu (JJ) automatically.
evidence.claim: Supports viewing diffs for multiple version control systems

evidence.quote: Antigravity CLI scopes conversation histories directly to your current working directory. When you launch agy from a specific directory, the agent only displays and resumes sessions associated with that specific local repository or subdirectory.
evidence.claim: Workspace scoping limits context to local repository directories
